content: Minocycline is a medication used to treat moderate to severe acne in individuals aged 12 years and older. It works by reducing the number of pimples and belongs to a class of drugs known as tetracycline antibiotics. This antibiotic targets acne caused by bacterial infections but is ineffective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. When taking minocycline, follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. It is typically taken orally once daily, with or without food. Swallow the medication whole without crushing or chewing it. Take each dose with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Avoid lying down for at least 10 minutes after taking the medication to reduce the risk of esophageal irritation. For this reason, do not take it right before bedtime. Additionally, avoid consuming products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate (e.g., antacids, dairy products, or calcium-enriched juice) within 2 to 3 hours before or after taking minocycline, as these can interfere with its absorption. To achieve the best results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not skip doses, as this may reduce its effectiveness. Common side effects of minocycline include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, lightheadedness, or a sensation of spinning. While these effects are generally mild, contact your doctor if they persist or worsen. Symptoms of intracranial hypertension include persistent headaches, vision changes, or nausea. If this occurs, stop the medication and seek medical attention immediately, as it may lead to permanent vision loss or blindness. Minocycline may also rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacterial infection (Clostridium difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Symptoms include persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, or blood/mucus in the stool. Prolonged or repeated use of minocycline may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Inform your doctor if you notice white patches in your mouth, changes in vaginal discharge, or other signs of infection. Children under 8 years old are more sensitive to the side effects of minocycline, particularly tooth discoloration, which can also occur in older children and young adults. Pregnant individuals should avoid using minocycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the medication passes into breast milk. It may also reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). Inform your healthcare provider about all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, as drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of minocycline or increase the risk of side effects. Store minocycline at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication, as taking expired minocycline can cause serious illness. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. In case of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or a poison control center (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S.). This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not share it with others. Regular lab tests (e.g., complete blood count, kidney, or liver function tests) may be required to monitor your progress while taking minocycline. Always consult your healthcare provider for personalized medical advice and complete information about this medication.
